record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For polycyclic groups given by polycyclic presentations, determine a global computational complexity analysis for the collection algorithm used to solve the word problem. In particular, can the complexity be bounded in terms of the input word, rather than depending on the absolute values of exponents that arise during the intermediate collection process?

evidence.quote: The collection algorithm is generally effective in practical applications, but its precise computational complexity remains unknown.
The resultant worst-case bound is in terms of the absolute values of all exponents occurring during the collection process, rather than the exponents of the input word.
Thus a global complexity analysis of the collection algorithm remains elusive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a polycyclic group given by a polycyclic presentation
$$G = \langle g_1, \dots, g_n \mid g_i^{g_j} = w_{ij}\ (i>j),\ g_i^{g_j^{-1}} = w'_{ij}\ (i>j),\ g_i^{e_i} = u_i\ \text{for } i \in I \rangle,$$
where each $w_{ij}, w'_{ij}, u_i$ is a normal-form word $g_{i+1}^{a_{i+1}}\cdots g_n^{a_n}$, and the relative orders $e_i$ (for $i\in I$) are positive integers. Every element of $G$ has a unique normal form $g_1^{a_1}\cdots g_n^{a_n}$ with $0\le a_i<e_i$ when $i\in I$. The collection algorithm rewrites an arbitrary word $w$ in the generators into this normal form by repeated application of the power and conjugation relations, and thereby solves the word problem.

Carry out a global computational complexity analysis of the collection algorithm. Specifically, produce an upper bound on the worst-case running time of the collection algorithm that is expressed solely in terms of the input word $w$ (e.g., its length and the absolute values of the exponents appearing in $w$), together with the data of the fixed polycyclic presentation, rather than in terms of the absolute values of the exponents that arise in the intermediate words produced during the collection process.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is known: Gebhardt's "Efficient Collection in Infinite Polycyclic Groups" (J. Symbolic Comput. 2002) gives improved bounds in terms of exponents arising during collection, and more recent work (e.g. Shpilrain et al., 2024–2025) shows the word problem in any polycyclic group has worst-case complexity O(n log² n) using matrix representations, with linear average-case complexity. However, a tight global worst-case complexity analysis of the standard collection algorithm bounded purely in terms of the input word does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Collection in Infinite Polycyclic Groups
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm for collection in polycyclic groups has better complexity in terms of the exponents occurring in the collected words.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds for collection are typically given in terms of exponents in intermediate collected words.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of some algorithmic problems in groups: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: In any polycyclic group, the worst-case time complexity of the word problem is O(n log² n).
status_evidence.claim: The word problem in polycyclic groups admits a near-linear worst-case algorithm via matrix representations, though not via direct collection.

status_evidence.title: Linear average-case complexity of algorithmic problems in groups
status_evidence.snippet: Average-case time complexity of the word problem in polycyclic groups is linear.
status_evidence.claim: Average-case complexity is well understood; worst-case for collection itself remains less precisely characterized.
